claim: ServiceNow announced AI Passport for signed, runtime-scoped authority over AI agents and MCP servers.
verifiedFacts: On October 15 ServiceNow announced AI Passport with cryptographically signed credentials and per-agent scope verification; it is described as a new solution, not independently verified as generally deployed.
ServiceNow named NVIDIA as a design and launch partner for enforcement via its agent safety platform; announced governance includes discovery, access mapping, revocation, and audit.
inference: Inference: authorization at execution time could complement Seed Loom evidence acceptance, but Seed Loom should not become an enterprise identity product.
Consultancy implication: offer a bounded agent authorization/trace audit; client problem is agent access drifting beyond approved data, tools and tasks.
Disposition: Seed Loom CORE for knowledge boundaries; Agent Runtime Control Center CONSOLIDATE candidate for runtime controls, keeping identities separate.
Thesis: strengthens the governed execution thesis rather than proving external consulting demand.
significance: A vendor and infrastructure partner are investing in runtime scope enforcement, a concrete external architecture to compare with human-controlled agent handoffs.
assumptions: Cryptographic authorization can be integrated with heterogeneous agent runtimes.
Vendor-stated controls function as described outside demos.
knownLimitations: Product availability and independent enforcement test results are unverified.
No client procurement for consultancy has been observed.
